sections.title: Iran War: Strike Talk Intensifies
sections.summary: Trump floats 'another little Epic Fury'; Iran threatens Gulf undersea cables if war resumes

paragraphs.heading: Mixed signals
paragraphs.body: US envoy Tom Barrack, asked whether the US could strike Iran this weekend, said 'Absolutely', while stressing Trump remains open to a deal. Trump said 'If that's the case, I don't know anything about it', then told a Florida rally 'we may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree', according to The National, NTD and Türkiye Today. The White House has said there will be no attack before the November 3 midterms. [[TAG:danger:mixed signals]]

paragraphs.heading: Netanyahu's directive
paragraphs.body: Netanyahu said he had directed the IDF and Mossad to overthrow Iran's regime, citing Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei's pursuit of weapons, The Jerusalem Post and Foreign Policy reported. He claimed Trump had said the US was ready to 'finish the job'. Defense Minister Israel Katz warned 'Iran will burn' if it attacks Israel.

paragraphs.heading: Cable threat
paragraphs.body: Two senior Iranian security officials told Reuters that Tehran has contingency plans to attack undersea communications cables in the Persian Gulf if the US and Israel strike again, and to obstruct repairs, the Times of Israel and Baird Maritime reported. Analysts said less than 1% of international bandwidth passes through Hormuz, so effects would be mainly regional. [[TAG:warning:cable risk]]

paragraphs.heading: Blockade at 100 days
paragraphs.body: CENTCOM marked 100 days of its naval blockade of Iranian ports, which it says has cut off billions of dollars in crude shipments, NBC News reported. Iran says the strait would reopen within six days if the US lifts the blockade, and it warned that the US military is not allowed in the Gulf 'under any circumstance', CBS News reported. US UN Ambassador Mike Waltz said the war could last another year.

paragraphs.heading: Attack wave
paragraphs.body: The Houthis claimed attacks over 48 hours on Abha airport, the Saudi defense ministry in Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu, Asharq Al-Awsat reported. The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed a ballistic missile heading toward Najran and nine drones aimed at the Eastern Province, Riyadh and Medina. paragraphs.heading: UN concern

sections.title: Ukraine and Russia
sections.summary: Oleshky truce credited to Melania Trump; 270-for-270 swap; Kyiv disputes Starlink fix

paragraphs.heading: Oleshky ceasefire
paragraphs.body: Russia and Ukraine agreed a localized ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky to allow aid deliveries, demining and civilian evacuations, which the White House said Melania Trump brokered by working directly with both governments, NBC News and The Globe and Mail reported. The White House said it begins October 29; Ukraine's ombudsman told Reuters October 27. [[TAG:success:local truce]]

paragraphs.heading: Prisoner swap
paragraphs.body: The two sides exchanged 270 servicemen each, the first swap since August, and Russia's Defense Ministry said 120 civilians were also included, The Moscow Times reported. Putin said future talks should focus on security guarantees for both countries and a European security framework.

paragraphs.heading: Starlink dispute
paragraphs.body: Trump said Elon Musk had restored Ukraine's Starlink access, but Ukrainian officials said restrictions remain, including a 161 km/h speed cap, The Washington Post and the Kyiv Independent reported. The Wall Street Journal reported Trump called Musk on October 21 asking him to lift the limits. [[TAG:warning:still restricted]]

sections.summary: Cook: GOP House path 'all but evaporated' after 19 ratings shift; Trump stumps in Florida

paragraphs.heading: House outlook
paragraphs.body: The Cook Political Report shifted 19 House races toward Democrats and now favors Democrats in 220 districts, Republicans in 198, with 17 toss-ups, Yahoo News and Newsweek reported. Cook said the Republican path to holding the House 'has all but evaporated', CNN reported; Cook has moved 63 ratings toward Democrats in a month. [[TAG:danger:220 seats lean D]]

paragraphs.heading: Florida rally
paragraphs.body: Trump rallied in Fort Myers, announcing $275 million in federal funding to hire nurses for senior care, and said he has spent $300 million on midterm ads with $100 million more planned, Fox News reported. Speaker Mike Johnson is asking Trump for more money, CNN reported. CNN is threatening legal action after its journalists were denied Air Force One access, NPR reported.

sections.title: Europe
sections.summary: Macron curbs 'illegitimate' protests as 70,000 police deploy; heat waves killed 50,000, study says

paragraphs.heading: France tightens curbs
paragraphs.body: Macron said local authorities would ban gatherings by groups deemed to lack legitimacy while allowing union-organized marches on possibly diverted routes, blaming 'ultra-left' groups for recent riots, NBC News and Reuters via US News reported. Protests were banned in Paris, Lyon, Lille and Grenoble, and Fox News reported 70,000 police deployed for the weekend. A union said Macron was 'trampling' the right to protest. Accounts differ on how sweeping the measures are. [[TAG:warning:protest bans]]

paragraphs.heading: Elsewhere
paragraphs.body: A study estimated this summer's European heat waves killed about 50,000 people, attributing two-thirds of deaths to climate change, Democracy Now reported. The European Commission is weighing tougher measures on Chinese imports, Euronews reported, and Serbia heads toward a snap election.

sections.title: Elections Abroad
sections.summary: Israel's final polls: Eisenkot ahead, no majority; Brazil runoff Sunday is a statistical tie

paragraphs.heading: Israel
paragraphs.body: Final TV polls from Kan, Channel 12 and Channel 13 put Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar ahead of Likud, with Netanyahu's bloc at about 50 seats and the opposition at 52 to 56, short of 61, Ynet reported. Jewish Insider's average instead puts Netanyahu's bloc ahead at 54. Arab parties are projected at 14 to 16 seats. Netanyahu cancelled Friday campaign events after a West Bank shooting attack, Haaretz reported. Israel votes Tuesday. [[TAG:warning:deadlock]]

paragraphs.heading: Brazil
paragraphs.body: Datafolha has Flávio Bolsonaro and President Lula tied at 50% of valid votes ahead of Sunday's runoff, Bloomberg reported, and The Rio Times' average gives Bolsonaro about 51%. Prediction markets give Bolsonaro about 80% odds. Flávio finished first in the October 4 first round, against most polls' predictions. [[TAG:info:Sunday runoff]]

sections.summary: Kim Jong Un crosses new bridge into China; US tightens Ebola entry screening

paragraphs.heading: Kim in China
paragraphs.body: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un traveled to China across the newly opened bridge at Dandong and met Premier Li Qiang, a South Korean official told Reuters, according to The Standard and Al Jazeera. The visit comes just before the anniversary of China's entry into the Korean War. [[TAG:info:Kim visits China]]

paragraphs.heading: Ebola screening
paragraphs.body: The US will require air travelers to declare they have not been in Congo in the previous 21 days, NBC News reported, while keeping entry bans for foreign nationals recently in Uganda or South Sudan. Congo and South Sudan are strengthening cross-border surveillance with WHO support, and the UN named a senior Ebola coordinator based in Bunia, OCHA said.
